sources: 1.13.2 server.jar brigadier ArgumentTypes registration order (class-file scan; no Java runtime required)
_provenance.note: the version's OWN brigadier argument-type registry, in registration order, read out of the server jar. Before 1.19 a command-tree argument node names its parser with a resource-location STRING, so these names ARE the wire and the 'id' here is a table index only, not a wire id (numeric parser ids arrive at 1.19). This table used to be built by walking minecraft-data's commands.json and alphabetising the parser strings it found, which was wrong three times over. The upstream tree carries 1.19-era names (nbt_compound_tag and nbt_tag instead of 1.13's single nbt, plus time, uuid and angle, which are 1.14, 1.16 and 1.16.2 additions). A tree walk can only ever see the parsers vanilla COMMANDS USE, never the ones merely REGISTERED, which is how minecraft:float_range went missing on every band. And it produced one identical table for all three bands, which cannot be right: 1.13.1 added minecraft:column_pos and minecraft:dimension, so 393 has 37 entries where 401 and 404 have 39. Cross-checked against each version's own data-generator reports/commands.json: every parser vanilla's command tree uses appears here, and the only registered-but-unused entry on all three bands is minecraft:float_range.
